# Phenotype and function of GM-CSF independent dendritic cells generated by long-term propagation of rat bone marrow cells.
**Authors:** Yan H, Miyagi T, Satoh E, Sugiura W, Yamamoto N, Kimura H
**Journal:** Cell Immunol (2004)
**DOI:** [10.1016/j.cellimm.2004.07.006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cellimm.2004.07.006)

## Abstract

1. Cell Immunol. 2004 Jun;229(2):117-29. doi: 10.1016/j.cellimm.2004.07.006.

Phenotype and function of GM-CSF independent dendritic cells generated by
long-term propagation of rat bone marrow cells.

Yan H(1), Miyagi T, Satoh E, Sugiura W, Yamamoto N, Kimura H.

Author information:
(1)Department of Research Surgery, National Center for Child Health and
Development, Tokyo, Japan.

GM-CSF is believed to be an essential factor for growth and differentiation of
myeloid dendritic cells (DC). Employing a low-density fraction of rat bone
marrow cells, we attempted to generate DC with human Flt-3/Flk-2 and IL-6. In
this culture system, typical DC gradually appeared without exogenous GM-CSF
supplement. Phenotypes and functions of the DC were examined. Evidence provided
that the most efficient long-term outgrowth of DC progenitors was obtained by
GM-CSF independent culture systems with the aid of Flt3/Flk-2 and IL-6, not with
c-kit ligand and IL-6. Furthermore, CD103 (OX-62), which is widely used for rat
DC separation, was found to be insufficient for enriching DC, due to the
down-regulation of the marker. However, the most efficient selection of rat DC
was made by CD161a (NKR-P1A), a C-type lectin family. The GM-CSF independent DC
was functionally active in vitro as well as in vivo assays.
